value.body: Companies that make Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani and Homoeopathy (ASU&H) medicines, supplements and personal-care products hire Ayush graduates for product development, quality control, regulatory work, medical advisory and sales-support roles. The work uses your knowledge of classical formulations and drug standards rather than clinical practice. These are private-sector jobs and conditions vary by company size.

items.label: Governing law
items.note: Chapter IVA and related rules cover Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani drugs

items.label: Licensing
items.note: Under the Ministry of Ayush framework; drug standards set by the Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A BAMS, BHMS, BSMS or BUMS degree, usually with registration with the state board or council. Hiring is direct by companies; there is no common entrance test. Some technical roles under the drug rules require a specified qualification and experience, which varies by role and state.

value.title: At a glance
items: Typical roles: product development, QA/QC, regulatory affairs, medical advisor, clinical research and medical representative.
Large manufacturers are concentrated in a few states; many small units offer limited structured training.
Regulatory and quality roles reward familiarity with pharmacopoeial standards and GMP documentation.
Some graduates combine industry work with part-time practice; check employer rules first.
